text:
City Boy Care has extended its social welfare and community intervention outreach to expectant and nursing mothers in Benin City, Edo State, with the distribution of ‘Mama & Child Kits’ and financial assistance towards the settlement of selected outstanding hospital bills at the Edo Specialist Hospital, Benin.
The outreach, aimed at strengthening maternal and child welfare, occasioned the provision of essential items and practical support to pregnant women, nursing mothers and their families.
Speaking during the exercise, the Director of City Boy Care, Omowunmi Imoukhuede, said the initiative reflected the commitment to compassion, social welfare and improving the lives of Nigerians through practical interventions that address real community needs, beyond political and electoral considerations.
She attributed the vision behind the intervention to the Patron of the City Boy Movement, Mr Seyi Tinubu, noting that the initiative reflects the values of love, solidarity and service by translating them into meaningful support for individuals, families and communities.
Imoukhuede explained that City Boy Care is a social welfare and community intervention system within the broader City Boy ecosystem, designed to connect individuals and communities with access to structured benefits, essential support and opportunities.
She highlighted that its benefits portfolio is organised around six categories: Health and Care; Food and Essential Support; Digital Access and Inclusion; Education and Learning Support; Livelihoods and Economic Opportunities; and Community Development.
She further explained that the Mama & Child Kit is a benefit product under the Health and Care category of the City Boy Care Benefits Portfolio. It forms part of broader efforts to support families throughout pregnancy, childbirth and early childcare, ensuring that mothers and their children have access to essential items and support during these important stages of life.
The outreach was organised in collaboration with the Edo State chapter of the City Boy Movement, with Pipeline Infrastructure Nigeria Limited serving as the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) partner, supporting the execution of the day’s activities.
As part of the exercise, a registration and verification centre was established within the hospital to facilitate the enrolment of beneficiaries on the City Boy Care platform.
The platform is designed to connect individuals and communities with relevant benefit products, social welfare interventions and various opportunities.
The delegation also visited expectant mothers attending antenatal services, nursing mothers and patients receiving inpatient care.
Financial assistance was equally extended towards the settlement of selected outstanding hospital bills through the hospital’s Social Welfare Department.
Speaking on the initiative, the Edo State Coordinator of the City Boy Movement and the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Oredo Federal Constituency, Dr. Paddy Iyamu, reaffirmed the movement’s commitment to people-oriented engagements that promote social welfare and community development.
Iyamu emphasised that the movement’s community engagements were driven by a genuine desire to improve lives, respond to the needs of communities and support meaningful development, rather than electoral considerations or the pursuit of votes.
In her remarks, the Chief Medical Director of Edo Specialist Hospital, Dr. Anthonia Inibokun Njoku, commended the City Boy Care team, particularly its young volunteers, for their dedication and commitment to social welfare.
She encouraged them to sustain the initiative, describing their efforts as commendable and worthy of emulation by other young people.
City Boy Care expressed appreciation to Pipeline Infrastructure Nigeria Limited, the management of Edo Specialist Hospital, healthcare professionals, volunteers and members of the Edo State chapter of the City Boy Movement for their contributions to the successful execution of the outreach.
One of the beneficiaries, Mrs. Blessing Osebor, expressed gratitude to the organisers, describing the support as timely and impactful.
She also offered prayers for safe deliveries and healthy babies for all expectant mothers.
